applies_why: The text weighs the challenger's chain against the defender's chain in a link-versus-link collision (D6 vs C1), which is exactly the chain-against-chain footing contest this rule governs.
quote: the challenger's seed/loins chain is footed but does not name Joseph as the begetter
rule_words: A link is judged by its support, never by whether any verse, or the chain as a whole, states it word for word; that no one of them states the contrary in its own words is the stating-verse test DG-61 retires, at a judge's seat as at a debater's, for either side.
room: Phrase weighed: 'does not name Joseph as the begetter.' Reading one: the judge let the footed chain's lack of an explicit statement count against it, which is the retired stating-verse test. Reading two: the judge merely noted the chain makes no claim about the begetter's identity, a footing-scope observation. I chose reading one because the judge's 'but' frames the non-naming as a deficiency weighed against a chain the judge already pronounced footed.
why: Having found the challenger's chain footed, the judge still held its failure to state Joseph as the begetter in its own words against it, using the very stating-verse test K-C retires for either side instead of weighing by footing alone.
